description: The military dimension: Chinese arms supplies to both sides of the conflict, PMCs/PSCs in the DRC
verification_status: drone and air-defense supplies are confirmed by industry and news sources; the specific claim about CH-4s being intercepted by Sky Dragon systems originates from DRC intelligence and is not independently verified

ch4_caihong4.manufacturer: CASC (China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation)
ch4_caihong4.delivery: three batches of 3 units, the last in May 2024
ch4_caihong4.use: reconnaissance and strikes on M23/RDF positions in eastern DRC

wing_loong_2.status: under negotiation, not finalized as of the last check (April 2025)

models_under_negotiation: Chengdu FC-1 Xiaolong / JF-17 (joint with Pakistan)
fighter_jets.context: replacing Soviet-era Su-25s (one damaged by a missile at Goma airport, 2023)
fighter_jets.verification_status: not independently re-verified this round - carried over from the user's original document

sky_dragon_50_tl_50_dk_10.manufacturer: Norinco (China North Industries Corporation) / AVIC development
sky_dragon_50_tl_50_dk_10.status: Rwanda was the first foreign buyer of the system

yitian.verification_status: mentioned in the context of Chinese air-defense systems in the region; a specific delivery to Rwanda has not been independently confirmed

china_supplies_to_rwanda.interception_claim: according to DRC intelligence (citing Africa Intelligence, per the user's original document), Rwanda uses Sky Dragon 50 against DRC's CH-4 drones - this specific claim was not confirmed by an independent source during verification and is noted as one party's allegation

private_military_and_security.name: Chinese PSCs (general)
private_military_and_security.mandate: perimeter and logistics security for mines in the south (Lualaba, Haut-Katanga), no combat role
private_military_and_security.distinction_from_wagner: not aimed at political control or frontline operations

private_military_and_security.name: Frontier Services Group (FSG) / Erik Prince
private_military_and_security.contract: with the DRC Ministry of Finance, April 2025
private_military_and_security.mandate: tax collection, anti-smuggling of minerals, security in Katanga; initially no combat role envisioned
private_military_and_security.escalation: February 2026 - Prince's contractors provided support (including drones) to DRC forces defending Uvira from M23; reverted to tax/security functions after the situation stabilized
private_military_and_security.historical_context: structures linked to Prince (Cheetah Logistics) had already operated in the DRC since 2015; FSG has historic ties to China's CITIC

private_military_and_security.name: Agemira RDC
private_military_and_security.function: reportedly services/logistics for DRC drones, airfield security
private_military_and_security.verification_status: not independently re-verified this round - carried over from the user's original document

private_military_and_security.name: Congo Protection (Romanian contractors)
private_military_and_security.verification_status: not independently re-verified this round - carried over from the user's original document; a broader, separately confirmed fact (Military Africa, 2025) is that Rwanda/M23 forces captured over 200 European mercenaries in February, including Romanians who had been fighting on the DRC side

conflict_context.sides: FARDC plus allied militias (Wazalendo) against M23 (which UN reporting says is backed by Rwanda)
conflict_context.china_un_security_council_position: non-interference rhetoric; support for ceasefire and withdrawal resolutions; blocks initiatives linking market access to human rights
